channel.description: New and amended rules from Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, as covered by the Financial Regulation Hub.

item.title: FEMA: Compounding of certain FEMA contraventions delegated to RBI Regional Offices
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 28/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-23.

Who it covers: Applicants compounding contraventions of the Borrowing and Lending Regulations, the Guarantees Regulations or the overseas investment framework.

  • Borrowing and lending, and guarantee, contraventions are compounded by the Regional Office with jurisdiction over the applicant's registered office.
  • Overseas investment cases go to one of seven Regional Offices by the prefix of the unique identification number; mixed cases stay with the Central Office.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Non-deliverable rupee derivatives for non-residents only for hedging; reserve on AD banks' own hedges
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 27/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-12.

Who it covers: AD banks with IFSC banking units, standalone primary dealers, and non-resident users.

  • AD banks may offer non-deliverable rupee derivatives to non-residents only for hedging.
  • A 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve applies to AD banks' own rupee hedges where they buy foreign currency.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: No rebooking of cancelled rupee derivatives; threshold without proof of exposure cut to USD 5 million
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-10.

Who it covers: Users hedging with AD banks, including ECB and trade credit borrowers, and AD banks.

  • Cancelled rupee derivatives may not be rebooked; rollovers on maturity are still allowed.
  • Positions without establishing the underlying exposure fall from USD 100 million to USD 5 million.
  • Users give an undertaking that the same exposure is not hedged with another AD bank.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve of 20% on rupee derivatives hedging current account payments
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-10.

Who it covers: AD banks and users buying foreign currency forward against rupees for current account transactions.

  • AD banks keep 20% of the rupee notional of each such contract above USD 2 million as cash with RBI until the contract ends.
  • Splitting deals to stay below the threshold is a violation.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Seven old FEMA circulars withdrawn, including ECB circulars on rupee bonds and rupee ECB
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 21/2026-27

Effective 2026-09-08.

Who it covers: AD banks and borrowers relying on older ECB circulars.

  • Withdrawn: ECB circulars on rupee denominated bonds overseas (2015), ECB in Indian rupees (2014), the infrastructure definition (2014), tax-free bonds bought by non-residents (2013), import of services (2013) and ECB by SIDBI (2012), plus one MTSS circular.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Deposit (Sixth Amendment) Regulations, 2026: SNRR accounts for any non-resident, including in IFSC
item.description:
FEMA · Amendment Regulations · FEMA 5(R)(6)/2026-RB

Effective 2026-06-29.

Who it covers: Non-residents doing rupee business in India, and AD banks.

  • Any person resident outside India may open an SNRR account with an AD bank in India or its branch outside India, including in an IFSC.
  • Transfers between NRO and NRE or SNRR accounts within the Remittance of Assets limit are allowed.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Daily reporting of ECBs raised under RBI's swap facility
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 15/2026-27

Effective 2026-06-19.

Who it covers: AD banks handling ECBs, FCNR(B) deposits and overseas foreign currency borrowings mobilised under RBI's June 2026 swap facility.

  • Daily data by 6 p.m., with a nil statement on days with no transactions.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: AD banks barred from rupee derivatives with related parties, with exceptions
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 7/2026-27

Effective 2026-04-20.

Who it covers: AD banks and their related parties.

  • Replaces the 1 April 2026 instructions.
  • No rupee derivatives with related parties, except cancellation and rollover of existing contracts and back-to-back deals with unrelated non-resident users.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: FPI debt limits for 2026-27; corporate bond limit stays at 15%
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 5/2026-27

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: Issuers of bonds and NCDs bought by FPIs, FPIs and custodians.

  • Corporate bond limit: Rs 9,36,113 crore for April-September 2026 and Rs 9,91,392 crore for October 2026-March 2027.
  • Voluntary Retention Route investments come under the General Route limits from 01-04-2026.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Overseas investment references to RBI moved to seven Regional Offices
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 2/2026-27

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: Indian entities lending to or guaranteeing for foreign entities, and AD banks.

  • References go through PRAVAAH to the Regional Office set by the UIN prefix (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Kolkata, New Delhi, Hyderabad or Chennai).

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Guarantee reporting forms GRN Issue, Modification and Invocation
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 1/2026-27

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: Residents who must report cross-border guarantees, and AD banks.

  • New GRN forms for issue, modification and invocation.
  • AD banks report on CIMS within 30 days of quarter-end and allot a Guarantee Transaction Number.
  • For the late fee, the amount is nil for issue and modification, and the surety's liability for invocation.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Late submission fee for ECB returns: per return, paid to the Regional Office
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25/2025-26

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: ECB borrowers and designated AD banks.

  • Form ECB 1 and Revised Form ECB 1 are returns that do not capture flows for the fee.
  • Each late Form ECB 2 is a separate instance.
  • AD banks forward returns within 7 calendar days and monitor payment; the fee is paid to the RBI Regional Office after RBI's email.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: New Form ECB 1 and Form ECB 2
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 23/2025-26

Effective 2026-02-18.

Who it covers: ECB borrowers and designated AD banks.

  • Form ECB 1 and Revised Form ECB 1 replace Form ECB; a new Form ECB 2 replaces the old return.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: New ECB framework: Borrowing and Lending (First Amendment) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
FEMA · Amendment Regulations · FEMA 3(R)(5)/2026-RB; A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 22/2025-26

Effective 2026-02-16.

Who it covers: All resident non-individual borrowers, non-resident lenders and AD banks.

  • Any non-individual resident incorporated or registered under a Central or State Act may borrow; any non-resident is a recognised lender.
  • Limit: higher of USD 1 billion outstanding or 300% of net worth, not applicable to entities regulated by a financial sector regulator.
  • Minimum average maturity of 3 years (1-3 years for manufacturers up to USD 150 million); cost at market terms.
  • A single end-use list in regulation 3A; RBI-regulated entities may not issue guarantees for ECBs.
  • ECBs registered earlier continue on their old terms except for reporting.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Voluntary Retention Route merged into the General Route from 01-04-2026
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 21/2025-26

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: FPIs, issuers and custodians.

  • FPI debt investment under the Voluntary Retention Route is governed by the General Route conditions from 01-04-2026.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Foreign Exchange Management (Guarantees) Regulations, 2026 in force
item.description:
FEMA · Regulations · FEMA 8(R)/2026-RB; A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 19/2025-26

Effective 2026-01-10.

Who it covers: Residents who are sureties, principal debtors or creditors in guarantees with a non-resident party, and AD banks.

  • Replace the Guarantees Regulations, 2000.
  • A resident may be surety or principal debtor if the underlying transaction is permitted and both are eligible to lend and borrow under the B&L Regulations.
  • Quarterly reporting within 15 days of quarter-end, and a late submission fee.
  • 19 older guarantee circulars withdrawn.

Official source
